about: Data for supply.py. rules: the words of each finding ({0} is the file). popular: well-known package names per registry, for the look-alike check: a name one letter away from one of these is reported, a name on the list never is. Add a name here when a real package you use is reported as a look-alike.

supply-no-lockfile.title: {0} has no lockfile
supply-no-lockfile.why: every install then takes the newest versions that fit: builds are not repeatable, and a bad release gets in unseen
supply-no-lockfile.fix: create the lockfile (npm install, composer update, uv lock, poetry lock, or == pins in requirements.txt) and commit it

supply-lock-ignored.title: git ignores the lockfile of {0}
supply-lock-ignored.why: the lockfile never reaches the repo, so other machines and the container build install whatever is newest
supply-lock-ignored.fix: take that line out of .gitignore and commit the lockfile

supply-floating.title: {0} has versions with no upper limit
supply-floating.why: *, latest, >= or no pin lets a new major version, or a hijacked release, in at the next install
supply-floating.fix: give each an upper limit (^1.2.3, ~1.2) or pin it (==1.2.3)

supply-source.title: {0} takes code from outside the official registry
supply-source.why: a git URL, a download link or a local path skips the registry: whoever controls that place controls the code you run
supply-source.fix: use a released version from the registry, or pin a full commit hash; if it is meant to be so, note it as an accepted risk

supply-registry.title: {0} has packages that do not come from the official registry
supply-registry.why: the lockfile says where each package is downloaded from: another host can serve other code under a known name
supply-registry.fix: check each one against the registry; if it is meant to be so, note it as an accepted risk

supply-install-script.title: {0} has packages that run code when they are installed
supply-install-script.why: an install script or plugin runs with your rights on every machine that installs it: poisoned packages use this
supply-install-script.fix: check that you expect each one; in CI and container builds try npm ci --ignore-scripts

supply-typosquat.title: {0} has a name one letter away from a well-known package: check the spelling
supply-typosquat.why: attackers publish look-alike names (typosquats) that run their code when installed
supply-typosquat.fix: compare it with the real name and correct it; if it is meant to be so, note it as an accepted risk

supply-licence.title: {0} has packages under GPL, AGPL or SSPL
supply-licence.why: these licences can oblige you to publish your own source code (this is not legal advice)
supply-licence.fix: check that this fits how you ship the app, or replace the package

supply-no-licence.title: {0} has packages with no licence stated
supply-no-licence.why: without a licence you have no stated right to use the code (this is not legal advice)
supply-no-licence.fix: look the licence up on the package's own page; replace the package if it has none

supply-no-integrity.title: {0} has packages with no integrity hash
supply-no-integrity.why: without the hash the installer cannot tell that a download was changed on the way
supply-no-integrity.fix: run npm install again so the lockfile gets the hashes, and commit it
